source_block.parva: Shanti Parva, Rajadharmanushasana sub-parva (vulgate §53–§59, §67, §88; BORI CE 12.53–12.59, 12.67, 12.89): the return to Bhishma's bedside; Krishna and Bhishma on who should teach; Yudhishthira's shame and Bhishma's reassurance; the first lessons of rajadharma — exertion and truth, the king as a mother, the law of the fishes, gentle taxation like the bee
source_block.bori: BORI CE Shanti Parva, Rajadharmanushasana sub-parva, Debroy translation vol. 8: 12.53 (the return to Kurukshetra), 12.54 (Bhishma free of pain; Krishna on Bhishma's lasting fame), 12.55 (Yudhishthira's shame and fear of a curse; a kshatriya's dharma; 'ask without fear'), 12.56 (exertion over destiny; truth; the king as an expectant mother), 12.58–59 (sunset, the Drishadvati, the daily return), 12.67 (without a king, fish devour fish), 12.89.4–5 (revenue like honey from flowers; as gently as a leech).
source_block.gita_press: Gita Press Gorakhpur Mahabharata (Hindi, vulgate): Shanti Parva, Rajadharmanushasana Parva adhyayas 53–56 (Bhishma ke paas aagman; Shri Krishna–Bhishma samvad; Yudhishthira ko nirbhay hokar poochhne ka aadesh; rajadharma ka aarambh, shloka 56.45–46 garbhini mata ki upama), 58–59 (suryast, Drishadvati snaan, punah aagman), 67–68 (raja ki avashyakata — badi machhliyan chhoti machhliyon ko; 12.68.16 in the online GP text), 89.4 (bhramara iva padapam).
source_block.divergence: Ganguli and the Gita Press vulgate agree on adhyaya numbers for §53–§59; for the later lessons the online Gita Press text runs one ahead in places (fish 12.68.16 vs Ganguli §67; bee GP/BORI 89 vs Ganguli §88) — cited both ways. BORI CE chapters are cited at chapter level. Condensed: Bhishma's long praise of Krishna and Krishna's praise of Bhishma (§54), the full list of kingly qualities in §56–§58, the story of Prithu and the origin of the word 'raja' (§59), Brihaspati's sayings, and the leech and milking similes beside the bee (§88). In the texts Satyaki and many rishis are also present, and Kripa is named at sunset; they are not drawn. The 'listen' line condenses many days of teaching (the Rajadharma runs to §130 and the whole Shanti Parva follows).
source_block.chosen: Gita Press + BORI/Debroy overlap: the return to Kurukshetra with Krishna; Bhishma freed of pain by Krishna's grace; 'why not teach him yourself' and Krishna's answer about Bhishma's fame; Yudhishthira's shame and fear of a curse; Bhishma's reassurance that righteous battle is a kshatriya's dharma, the touching of the feet, 'ask without fear'; exertion over fate and truth; the mother simile; the law of the fishes; the bee simile for taxes; the daily return at sunset. Ganguli for English wording.
